draft.exec:
You asked for a web app on Alibaba Cloud. For any public-facing application, slow responses or outages directly reduce user engagement and revenue.

This proposal places your application across two zones in Singapore, with edge caching, automatic scaling and managed storage and databases.

The result is a foundation that handles traffic changes without manual intervention. To size the components correctly, we need to know what kind of web app this is.

needs.need: Run a web application on Alibaba Cloud.
needs.quote: A web app on Alibaba Cloud
needs.answer: The design provides compute, database, storage and networking in Singapore across two zones. This gives you a working foundation to launch your application without building each layer yourself.

needs.need: Handle traffic changes without manual intervention.
needs.answer: Automatic scaling adjusts the number of servers based on load. This reduces the risk of slow responses during peaks and lowers costs when demand is quiet.

needs.need: Protect a public application from malicious requests.
needs.answer: The edge layer filters traffic before it reaches your servers. This lowers the chance that attacks disrupt service or compromise user data.

outcomes.title: Resilience across two zones
outcomes.text: Compute, load balancing, cache and database run in two separate zones. If one zone has an issue, traffic shifts to the other, reducing the chance of an outage affecting your users.

outcomes.title: Cost follows actual usage
outcomes.text: Base compute runs continuously while additional servers start only when load rises and stop when it falls. Storage and logs are paid by consumption, keeping spend aligned with real activity.

outcomes.title: Faster page loads globally
outcomes.text: Static files are cached at the edge near your users, and dynamic requests are accelerated. This reduces wait times, which typically improves user retention and conversion rates.

why.dns: Your users need a reliable way to reach the application domain. A managed authoritative DNS service removes the operational burden of running your own name servers and directs visitors to the edge layer.
why.esa: Public web applications face slow load times and malicious traffic. Placing caching, acceleration and security at the edge reduces latency for users and lowers the risk of attacks reaching your servers.
why.alb: Traffic must reach healthy servers across two zones without manual routing. An application load balancer distributes requests based on content paths, reducing the risk of overloading a single server.
why.ecs: You need full control over the operating system to run your web application. Virtual machines give your team a familiar environment to deploy code without changing how the application works.
why.ess: Web traffic rarely stays flat, and paying for peak capacity all day raises costs. Automatic scaling adds servers when load increases and removes them when it drops, aligning spend with demand.
why.tair: Users expect fast responses and staying logged in as they navigate. A managed in-memory cache keeps sessions and frequently read data close to the application, reducing database load and improving speed.
why.rds: Application data needs reliable storage with backups. A managed relational database with a standby in another zone reduces the effort your team spends on maintenance and lowers the risk of data loss.
why.oss: Uploaded files and static assets grow over time and fill up server disks. Dedicated object storage holds these files durably, letting your application servers focus only on processing logic.

tradeoffs.text: The design places all components in Singapore. If most users are far from this region, they may experience higher latency.
tradeoffs.mitigation: Confirm where your users are located so we can adjust the edge strategy or consider additional regions.

tradeoffs.text: Edge security filters traffic before it reaches your servers, but rules require tuning to avoid blocking legitimate users.
tradeoffs.mitigation: Start with monitoring mode to learn normal traffic patterns before enforcing blocks.

next: Schedule a session with the account team to estimate monthly costs once the application type and expected traffic are defined.
Confirm what kind of web app this is so we can validate the architecture against your specific workload.
Tell us where most of your users are located to verify if Singapore is the right region for your compute and database.
